name: Ladākh
summary_text: Reconstituted in 2019 from the former state of Jammu and Kashmir into a union territory without its own legislature, so trans-related policy depends on the central government (an RTI survey counts Ladakh among the 19 states/UTs with no transgender welfare body). Beyond this administrative framework the country dossier found no region-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern material enough to score separately (±0.02); assessed at the national score.

sources.title: India’s Transgender Rights Bill a Huge Setback | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is Human Rights Watch's March 2026 statement on India's Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, characterising it as a major setback to the 2014 NALSA self-identification right and the 2019 Act's protections.

sources.title: Transgender Bill: India parliament passes amendment to redefine transgender identity amid protests
sources.claim_summary: BBC report (26 March 2026) on the amendment bill narrowing trans self-identification, passed by both houses and pending presidential assent: it limits recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, makes board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery, and sparked protests; the Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw it, and critics (including activists Laxman Narayan Tripathi and Grace Banu) warn it excludes many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people.

Times of India (Kolkata, 18 August 2024): a transwoman travelling to an RG Kar Medical College protest alleges a railway-police constable groped her at Rabindra Sadan metro station as a 'gender check'; police denied it and filed a counter-FIR. Shared national source: it evidences the policing practice of treating trans appearance as a suspicion category, which recurs in checkpoints and transit spaces countrywide rather than in this unit specifically.
